away.name: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare

matchups.winner: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare
matchups.recap:
Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare put together the kind of game plan that makes a blowout look easy, riding Brock Purdy's 28.48 and Christian McCaffrey's 20.6 to a Bust Hike that never actually felt like one. Stefon Diggs chipped in 19.2, and even with Carnell Tate and Tucker Kraft doing their best Dutch Oven impression, the roster had enough Boss juice to cruise to a post hike scrub.

Rome-ans 10:9-10 got a Guide Rec from Travis Kelce and Omarion Hampton, but Justin Jefferson no-showed at 7.0 and Jameson Williams Walked on the alpine vegetation with a Beak 4.3, and no amount of Lamar Jackson magic was fixing that. The Lone Eagle never found an answer for Purdy's afternoon, and this one was Bushwhacking without a compass by halftime. Sticky buns on Sunday Morning belong to the other side entirely.

The Machine Knows got a Guide Rec from Josh Allen's 40.82 and coasted, though even the Boss weeks come with fine print — Javonte Williams ate his trail cheese and salami at 6.5, and Malik Nabers turned into a full Dutch Oven with 0.6 points. Didn't matter. When your quarterback single-handedly outscores the other team's whole roster, the rest is scenery, and this one turned into a post hike scrub without much sweat.

Catalina Wine Mixon is stuck on the Point and Back, dropping to 0-2 with a lineup that never found the trail. Trevor Lawrence walked on the alpine vegetation at 6.16, DK Metcalf looked like a stunned naval battle queen, and the Bucs D/ST barely showed up. Under 70 points two weeks running is a Chief Ron Voice situation: "I'm disappointed in you." The Chair Force never adjusted, and Trey McBride's 14.1 wasn't nearly enough cover for a team bushwhacking without a compass.

Chef Boyardee Stefanowicz got his Swimming Basic this week, smoking Harley Jarvis by 55.7 while running the whole operation like a Penis Eating Pike stalking chum. Dak Prescott went off for 29.76, Jonathan Taylor carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 27.2, and DeVonta Smith tacked on 22.7 just for flavor. This wasn't a game plan so much as a clinic, and somewhere in the celebration Chef found time to holler I want you to BRING DOWN THE ROOF because 134.56 points deserved a little noise.

Harley Jarvis, meanwhile, was Bushwhacking without a compass from kickoff. Ja'Marr Chase and Jalen Hurts did their part, but David Montgomery ate his trail cheese and salami with a Beak 3.4, and Dallas Goedert basically no-showed at 0.9. The whole roster looked stuck in the Sewards, out-schemed and out-adjusted all afternoon. A rough follow-up to Week 1, and the coaching search should probably start soon.

Funk that Junk squeaked out a Bust Hike, going on with Jaxon Smith-Njigba doing enough scary-good work to qualify as a Penis Eating Pike all by himself, dragging Drake Maye's stunned naval battle queen performance and Kyle Pitts's 2.0 dud across the finish line. Old balls didn't need a perfect plan, just enough juice from Ferguson and Breece Hall to survive a week where half the roster went bushwhacking without a compass.

Love Thy Naber had CeeDee Lamb going full Woodsman Chief with 31.3 and James Cook III chipping in like a pro, but Colston Loveland's 0.8 stinker and Jadarian Price's face-plant meant the team had their lunch eaten by Yellow Yellow everywhere else. Little Brother never adjusted the game plan and paid for it by 1.68, a margin so thin it should sting worse than it does. Two straight Beak finishes now — Love Thy Naber is stuck on the Point and Back with no signs of digging out.

The 46er treated this one like a formality, riding Amon-Ra St. Brown's 30.7 and Kenneth Walker III's 20.8 to a post hike scrub that never once felt in doubt. Joe Burrow chipped in 16.18 without breaking a sweat, and the whole operation had that unmistakable feel of a manager who scouted the matchup, trusted the process, and let the Island Gudge machinery do what it does. Every arrow found the bullseye.

55 Burgers, meanwhile, were Stuck in the Sewards from kickoff, with Justin Herbert's 7.88 landing nowhere near his 19.48 projection and Luther Burden III doing his best stunned naval battle queen impression at 4.7. Jahmyr Gibbs and the Patriots D/ST tried to hold the fort with 20.3 and 20.0, but Counsel never adjusted the game plan as the Beak points piled up around them. A 35.9-point margin doesn't happen by accident — it happens when one side ran a pig and back and the other just showed up.

Team Bradford didn't need a game plan so much as a Davante Adams appreciation society, and 35.5 points from him papered over a Bijan Robinson stat line that never showed up and a DJ Moore performance that finished in the negatives. The skipper still had all the arrows in the bullseye anyway, because when your WR1 goes nuclear, Courtland Sutton scoring 4.0 barely registers as an issue. Derrick Henry ran like a woodsman running to the camp store often enough to make the rest of the roster's Beak stretch irrelevant, and this one turned into a post hike scrub in a hurry.

Ricky Huns, meanwhile, is stuck on the Point and Back after another outing that never found its footing. Caleb Williams and Saquon Barkley both no-showed their projections by a mile, Barkley in particular delivering a stunned naval battle queen impression at 2.5 points, and Kyren Williams doing his best carrying the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike routine wasn't enough to cover for it. Two straight Beak finishes now, and the game plan looked bushwhacking without a compass from the opening kick.

headline: Chase Brown had a bad scare after all
